title: Google proposes a sleep phase to reduce continual-learning forgetting
dek: A dedicated consolidation phase attempts to integrate new information without degrading older model capabilities.
evidence: Google Research technical announcement; claims await reproduction outside reported settings
takeaway: Benchmark retention and adaptation jointly: new-fact accuracy is not valuable if it destroys existing competencies.

sections.title: Mechanism

bullets.detail: Continual parameter updates can cause catastrophic forgetting; in-context learning preserves new facts only while they remain in the prompt.
Google introduces a sleep-like consolidation phase that integrates acquired information across learning cycles, aiming to preserve earlier knowledge and improve reasoning.

paragraphs: Problem: Continual parameter updates can cause catastrophic forgetting; in-context learning preserves new facts only while they remain in the prompt.
Approach: Google introduces a sleep-like consolidation phase that integrates acquired information across learning cycles, aiming to preserve earlier knowledge and improve reasoning.

sections.title: Evaluation implications

bullets.detail: A model can appear better on recently introduced facts while regressing on established tasks. Claims of continual learning require both retention and adaptation measurements.

Build a sequential curriculum with frozen old-task probes, newly learned facts, interference cases, update compute and post-update calibration. Measure forgetting per stage rather than only final accuracy.

paragraphs: Trade-off: A model can appear better on recently introduced facts while regressing on established tasks. Claims of continual learning require both retention and adaptation measurements.

Test: Build a sequential curriculum with frozen old-task probes, newly learned facts, interference cases, update compute and post-update calibration. Measure forgetting per stage rather than only final accuracy.
